key_insight: PEARL combines reinforcement learning with differentiable physics and adjoint sensitivities to learn real-time optimal control policies with far fewer environment interactions.
engineering_relevance: The approach is promising for high-dimensional, parametric control problems where sample efficiency, scalability, and generalization across operating conditions are critical.
method: Uses an actor-adjoint training loop to compute policy gradients over short horizons.
Leverages automatic differentiation and neural-network approximations of future returns to incorporate physics-based sensitivities.
Targets differentiable dynamical systems to reduce exploration burden and stabilize long-horizon learning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on two challenging parametric navigation problems in unsteady flows, where PEARL outperforms state-of-the-art RL while using fewer interactions and generalizing across scenarios.
watch_item: Performance depends on access to differentiable dynamics and accurate sensitivity approximations, which may limit applicability to systems with non-differentiable or poorly modeled physics.
paper_title: Physics-enhanced reinforcement learning for real-time optimal control of dynamical systems
